text:
sofia: Heads up — multiple EU Dedicated customers reporting 504s to our private model endpoint via PrivateLink in eu-west-1 since ~06:30 UTC. They resolve to the interface endpoint ENIs but the connection resets. Any quick ideas?

kenji: Seeing elevated 5xx from LB -> interface endpoint in our telemetry. Did anyone touch endpoint SGs or route tables overnight?

alex: infra-bot posted an alert: "[infra-bot] vpce-conn-failure eu-west-1: 5xx spike detected"

infra-bot: ALERT: service: model-hosting - connection failures to vpce-0a1b2c in eu-west-1 (since 06:28 UTC)

maria: Quick checklist: DNS (private hosted zone + VPC association), endpoint SGs (ingress from client subnets/NAT EIPs), route tables (make sure subnets route to endpoints as expected). Also confirm cross-account acceptance if applicable.

kenji: I ssh'd into a customer bastion and ran dig. DNS resolves to two ENI IPs, but curl to those IPs fails with connection reset. Suspect SG blocking ephemeral ports or wrong source IP due to NAT.

sofia: Paste of what we saw from customer:

```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal
10.0.123.45
10.0.123.46

$ curl -v --resolve "api.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.0.123.45" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.123.45 (10.0.123.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake...
* Connection reset by peer
```

kenji: Root cause pattern we've seen before: interface endpoint ENIs use SGs to control ingress. If client traffic is SNATed by the customer's NAT gateway, the source IP will be the NAT EIP(s), not the original client SG. If endpoint SG only allows the client SG or a narrow CIDR, the NATed traffic will be rejected. Also, Private DNS for interface endpoints does not automatically traverse peering/TGW — resolver rules or inbound endpoints are required.

maria: Also double-check that the endpoint has "Enable DNS name" set and that the customer's VPC has DNS resolution+hostnames enabled. Common mistake: they rely on peering and expect our private hostname to resolve across peering without resolver rules.

alex: Another thing: if the customer changed NAT autoscaling overnight, their EIPs could have rotated. If we were working from an allowlist of EIPs on the endpoint SG (or vice versa), that would break traffic.

sofia: Proposed action items:
- kenji: confirm source IPs observed at customer NAT (pcap)
- maria: check our endpoint SG inbound rules and whether they reference specific EIPs/SG IDs
- alex: verify endpoint service acceptance for cross-account endpoints and check cloudtrail for any changes
- infra-bot: collect recent config changes (last 24h) for vpce-0a1b2c

maria: Sample commands to run for customers/devs:

```
# check endpoint network interfaces + SGs
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*vpce-0a1b2c*" --region eu-west-1

# check DNS from a host in their VPC
dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @169.254.169.253

# test connection directly to ENI IP
curl -v --resolve "api.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.0.123.45" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health
```

kenji: Mitigations for customers:
- Add NAT EIPs to endpoint SG allowlist (short-term)
- Better: avoid SNAT for intra-VPC PrivateLink traffic (place callers in subnets that route directly to endpoints)
- If using peering/TGW, set up Route 53 resolver rules or inbound endpoints for private DNS to work cross-VPC
- For cross-account endpoint services, ensure the consumer endpoint is accepted and the endpoint policy permits the actions

sre-oncall: Marking this P2 while we validate. If customer confirms EIP rotation -> escalate to assist with SG update.

sofia: Customer confirmed their NAT ASG changed EIPs during scaling and they had a narrow allowlist on the VPCE SG. They updated the SG to include the new EIPs and also created a resolver rule to forward the private domain across TGW. Service restored at 07:12 UTC :thumbsup:

kenji: Follow-ups:
- Create KB: "PrivateLink + NAT gotchas (EIPs, DNS, peering/TGW)"
- Add diagnostic snippet to our runbook (dig/curl/traceroute + what to check in VPCE SG)
- Consider adding a check in onboarding checklist for Dedicated customers that use TGW/peering + NAT (we should advise on preferred subnet placement)

maria: I'll draft the KB and drop here when ready.

alex: Nice catch, team. Closing once KB linked.

infra-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: vpce-0a1b2c eu-west-1 - service reachable again (downtime ~44m)
